# Core
library(tidyverse)
library(rsample)
library(yardstick)
library(broom)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Modeling
library(mgcv)      # gam()
library(recipes)   # optional preprocessing for CV folds

Loading in the data

We’ll use the same Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC) data as last time. Each row is a patient. Outcome Diagnosis is Benign or Malignant. Predictors are 30 numeric features derived from FNA images.

# Download from UCI ML repo
  url_data  <- "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/breast-cancer-wisconsin/wdbc.data"
  raw <- read.csv(url_data, header = FALSE)


# According to UCI:
# V1 = ID, V2 = Diagnosis (M/B), V3:V32 = 30 features
names(raw) <- c("ID","Diagnosis",
                "radius_mean","texture_mean","perimeter_mean","area_mean","smoothness_mean",
                "compactness_mean","concavity_mean","concave_points_mean","symmetry_mean","fractal_dimension_mean",
                "radius_se","texture_se","perimeter_se","area_se","smoothness_se",
                "compactness_se","concavity_se","concave_points_se","symmetry_se","fractal_dimension_se",
                "radius_worst","texture_worst","perimeter_worst","area_worst","smoothness_worst",
                "compactness_worst","concavity_worst","concave_points_worst","symmetry_worst","fractal_dimension_worst")

bc <- raw %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(Diagnosis = factor(Diagnosis, levels = c("B","M"))) %>%  # B=negative (benign), M=positive (malignant)
  select(-ID)

Train/test split (stratified):

set.seed(42)
split <- initial_split(bc, prop = 0.8, strata = Diagnosis)
train <- training(split)
test  <- testing(split)

nrow(train); nrow(test)
## [1] 454
## [1] 115

Note: mgcv::gam() can handle predictors on their original scale. Standardization is not required, but we’ll use the same recipe within CV folds to avoid leakage when needed.

Optional base recipe for CV folds (zero-variance removal + standardization):

  rec_base <- recipe(Diagnosis ~ ., data = train) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_normalize(all_predictors())

⸻

Baseline GLM vs. GAM (smooths on key predictors)

We’ll compare a logistic GLM (linear terms) to a logistic GAM with smooth terms on a few influential predictors. We’ll also try a tensor interaction between radius_mean and texture_mean.

# Choose a compact set to make plots readable (you can expand later)
core_vars <- c("radius_mean","texture_mean","perimeter_mean","area_mean",
               "smoothness_mean","concavity_mean","concave_points_mean")

form_glm <- as.formula(
  paste("Diagnosis ~", paste(core_vars, collapse = " + "))
)

form_gam <- Diagnosis ~ 
  s(radius_mean, k = 10) +
  s(texture_mean, k = 10) +
  s(perimeter_mean, k = 10) +
  s(area_mean, k = 10) +
  s(smoothness_mean, k = 10) +
  s(concavity_mean, k = 10) +
  s(concave_points_mean, k = 10)

form_gam_te <- Diagnosis ~ 
  s(radius_mean, k = 10) +
  s(area_mean, k = 10) +
  te(radius_mean, area_mean, k = c(10,10)) +   # smooth interaction surface
  s(texture_mean, k = 10) +
  s(perimeter_mean, k = 10) +
  s(smoothness_mean, k = 10) +
  s(concavity_mean, k = 10) +
  s(concave_points_mean, k = 10)

# Fit on training data
glm_fit <- glm(form_glm, data = train, family = binomial())
## Warning: glm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred
gam_fit <- gam(form_gam, data = train, family = binomial(), method = "REML")
gam_te_fit <- gam(form_gam_te, data = train, family = binomial(), method = "REML")

-logLik(glm_fit)
## 'log Lik.' 62.27839 (df=8)
summary(gam_fit)$sp.criterion[1]   # REML score
##     REML 
## 44.31101
summary(gam_te_fit)$sp.criterion[1]
##     REML 
## 42.28213

Interpreting the gam.check() Table

The gam.check() output includes a table with columns like:

  • k’: the basis dimension you set in s(x, k=…). This is the maximum wiggliness allowed.

  • edf (effective degrees of freedom): how complex the fitted smooth actually is.

    • edf ≈ 1 → the effect is nearly linear.
    • edf > 1 → evidence of a nonlinear relationship.

  • k-index: checks whether the chosen k was large enough.

    • Close to 1 → fine.
    • Much lower than 1 → the model wanted more wiggle; k may be too small.

  • p-value: test of whether increasing k would improve the fit.

    • Small p-value (< 0.05) → increase k for that smooth.
    • Large p-value → current basis dimension is likely adequate.

Rule of thumb:
If the k-index is low and the p-value is small, refit with a larger k. Otherwise, your choice of k is probably fine.

Hold-out performance (AUC, sensitivity, specificity, NPV)

Predict on test set and compare GLM vs. GAM(s).

Helper: compute metrics at a fixed threshold (e.g., 0.5); AUC is threshold-free

eval_bin <- function(df_truth, probs, thr = 0.5) {
  cls <- factor(ifelse(probs >= thr, "M","B"), levels = levels(df_truth))
  tibble(
    AUC  = roc_auc_vec(df_truth, probs, event_level = "second"),
    Sens = sens_vec(df_truth, cls, event_level = "second"),
    Spec = spec_vec(df_truth, cls, event_level = "second"),
    NPV  = npv_vec (df_truth, cls, event_level = "second")
  )
}

p_test_glm   <- predict(glm_fit, newdata = test, type = "response")
p_test_gam   <- predict(gam_fit, newdata = test, type = "response")
p_test_gamte <- predict(gam_te_fit, newdata = test, type = "response")

bind_rows(
  eval_bin(test$Diagnosis, p_test_glm)   %>% mutate(Model = "GLM (linear)"),
  eval_bin(test$Diagnosis, p_test_gam)   %>% mutate(Model = "GAM (additive)"),
  eval_bin(test$Diagnosis, p_test_gamte) %>% mutate(Model = "GAM (additive + tensor)")
) %>%
  relocate(Model) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Hold-out performance (threshold = 0.5)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

CV selection among GLM and GAM candidates (by AUC)

We’ll do 10-fold stratified CV. Within each fold we’ll optionally standardize predictors via a recipe, fit competing models, and compute AUC on the validation partition.

set.seed(202)
folds <- vfold_cv(train, v = 10, strata = Diagnosis)

# Fold-wise evaluator for a provided fit function
cv_eval <- function(folds, base_recipe, fit_fun, pred_type = c("response","link")) {
  pred_type <- match.arg(pred_type)
  map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(folds)), function(i){
    sp <- folds$splits[[i]]
    tr <- analysis(sp); va <- assessment(sp)
    
    # fold-specific preprocessing
    rec <- prep(base_recipe, training = tr)
    trx <- bake(rec, tr)
    vax <- bake(rec, va)
    
    fit <- fit_fun(trx)
    p   <- predict(fit, newdata = vax, type = pred_type)
    # mgcv::predict returns numeric probs for binomial when type="response"
    tibble(fold = i, AUC = roc_auc_vec(vax$Diagnosis, p, event_level = "second"))
  }) %>% summarise(AUC_mean = mean(AUC), AUC_sd = sd(AUC))
}

fit_glm_fun <- function(dat) glm(form_glm, data = dat, family = binomial())
fit_gam_fun <- function(dat) gam(form_gam, data = dat, family = binomial(), method = "REML")
fit_gamte_fun <- function(dat) gam(form_gam_te, data = dat, family = binomial(), method = "REML")

cv_glm   <- cv_eval(folds, rec_base, fit_glm_fun,   pred_type = "response")

cv_gamte <- cv_eval(folds, rec_base, fit_gamte_fun, pred_type = "response")
## Warning in newton(lsp = lsp, X = G$X, y = G$y, Eb = G$Eb, UrS = G$UrS, L = G$L,

bind_rows(
  cv_glm   %>% mutate(Model = "GLM"),
  cv_gam   %>% mutate(Model = "GAM"),
  cv_gamte %>% mutate(Model = "GAM + tensor")
) %>% relocate(Model) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "10-fold CV by AUC (training folds only)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

Automatic smooth selection (select=TRUE) and concurvity check

mgcv can shrink smooths to zero if they’re not helpful (select=TRUE), similar in spirit to feature selection.
This adds an extra penalty to each term so that the smoothing parameter estimation can essentially remove terms from the model.

form_gam_sel <- Diagnosis ~ 
  s(radius_mean, k = 10) +
  s(texture_mean, k = 10) +
  s(perimeter_mean, k = 10) +
  s(area_mean, k = 10) +
  s(smoothness_mean, k = 10) +
  s(concavity_mean, k = 10) +
  s(concave_points_mean, k = 10)

gam_sel <- gam(form_gam_sel, data = train, family = binomial(), method = "REML", select = TRUE)
summary(gam_sel)
## 
## Family: binomial 
## Link function: logit 
## 
## Formula:
## Diagnosis ~ s(radius_mean, k = 10) + s(texture_mean, k = 10) +

##     k = 10) + s(concavity_mean, k = 10) + s(concave_points_mean, 
##     k = 10)
## 
## Parametric coefficients:

## ---

## 
## Approximate significance of smooth terms:
##                              edf Ref.df Chi.sq  p-value    
## s(radius_mean)         6.491e-06      9  0.000  0.60167    
## s(texture_mean)        2.611e+00      9 26.551 5.44e-07 ***
## s(perimeter_mean)      3.182e-05      9  0.000  0.15573    
## s(area_mean)           9.640e-01      9 22.932  < 2e-16 ***
## s(smoothness_mean)     8.920e-01      9  7.185  0.00213 ** 
## s(concavity_mean)      1.553e+00      9  3.981  0.04358 *  
## s(concave_points_mean) 7.675e-01      9  2.805  0.02937 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

# Concurvity (nonlinear analogue of multicollinearity)
conc <- concurvity(gam_sel, full = TRUE)
conc[3,-1] %>% 
  as_tibble(rownames = "term") %>% 
  arrange(desc(value)) %>%
  head(10) %>% 
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Top concurvity estimates (higher = more problematic)") %>% 
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

⸻

Calibrated threshold via Youden’s J (optional)

Pick a probability threshold on the training set (Youden’s J) and evaluate on the test set for the chosen GAM.

tune_threshold_j <- function(truth, prob, grid = seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01)) {
  stopifnot(is.factor(truth), length(levels(truth)) == 2)
  best_thr <- 0.5; best_j <- -Inf
  for (t in grid) {
    cls <- factor(ifelse(prob >= t, levels(truth)[2], levels(truth)[1]),
                  levels = levels(truth))
    se <- sens_vec(truth, cls, event_level = "second")
    sp <- spec_vec(truth, cls, event_level = "second")
    j  <- as.numeric(se + sp - 1)
    if (!is.na(j) && j > best_j) { best_j <- j; best_thr <- t }
  }
  best_thr
}

p_tr_gam <- predict(gam_sel, newdata = train, type = "response")
thr_gam  <- tune_threshold_j(train$Diagnosis, p_tr_gam)

p_te_gam <- predict(gam_sel, newdata = test, type = "response")
cls_te   <- factor(ifelse(p_te_gam >= thr_gam, "M","B"), levels = levels(test$Diagnosis))

tibble(
  Model = "GAM (select=TRUE)",
  Threshold = thr_gam,
  Test_AUC  = roc_auc_vec(test$Diagnosis, p_te_gam, event_level = "second"),
  Test_Sens = sens_vec(test$Diagnosis, cls_te,    event_level = "second"),
  Test_Spec = spec_vec(test$Diagnosis, cls_te,    event_level = "second"),
  Test_NPV  = npv_vec (test$Diagnosis, cls_te,    event_level = "second")
) %>% kable(digits = 3, caption = "GAM test performance at Youden-tuned threshold")
GAM test performance at Youden-tuned threshold
Model Threshold Test_AUC Test_Sens Test_Spec Test_NPV
GAM (select=TRUE) 0.49 0.997 0.93 0.986 0.959

⸻

Takeaways

• GAMs extend logistic regression by allowing smooth, nonlinear effects while keeping an additive structure.

• Tensor smooths (te()) capture interactions as smooth surfaces.

• Use REML (default here) for smoothness selection; select=TRUE can also shrink unhelpful smooths to zero.

• For model choice, prefer CV AUC; for deployment, tune a decision threshold (e.g., via Youden’s J) aligned with clinical goals.
